# TokyoLearn datasets

Static, versioned JSON datasets consumed by the Next.js app at build time. They are
generated by `scripts/fetch-jlpt-data.mjs` and validated against the TypeScript
interfaces in `src/types/japanese.ts`.

## Generated files

| File | Entries |
| --- | ---: |
| `kanji-n5.json` | 84 |
| `kanji-n4.json` | 169 |
| `kanji-n3.json` | 387 |
| `kanji-n2.json` | 398 |
| `kanji-n1.json` | 1,345 |
| `vocab-n5.json` | 674 |
| `vocab-n4.json` | 630 |
| `vocab-n3.json` | 1,659 |
| `vocab-n2.json` | 1,778 |
| `vocab-n1.json` | 3,070 |

Each file is a plain JSON array with one entry per line.

### Kanji entry

```ts
{
  character: string;
  jlpt: "N5" | "N4" | "N3" | "N2" | "N1";
  strokes: number;
  onyomi: string[];
  kunyomi: string[];
  meanings: string[];
  radicals: string[];
  examples: [
    { word: string; reading: string; meaning: string },
    { word: string; reading: string; meaning: string },
    { word: string; reading: string; meaning: string }
  ];
}
```

### Vocabulary entry

```ts
{
  word: string;
  reading: string;
  meaning: string;
  jlpt: "N5" | "N4" | "N3" | "N2" | "N1";
  partOfSpeech: string;
}
```

## Regenerate and verify

```bash
npm run fetch:data          # downloads sources (cached in .cache/jlpt) and writes /data
npm run fetch:data -- --refresh  # force re-download of all upstream sources
npm run verify:data         # TypeScript check + runtime schema validation
```

The generator prefers JLPT vocabulary as kanji examples, then JMdict common words,
then the kanji's own readings. A few rare name-only kanji have no dictionary words,
so their three examples are synthesized from the kanji's readings/senses.

## Sources and attribution

- [evanclan/OpenJLPT](https://github.com/evanclan/OpenJLPT) — cleaned Waller
  N5–N1 levels joined to JMdict/KANJIDIC2; CC BY-SA 4.0.
- [davidluzgouveia/kanji-data](https://github.com/davidluzgouveia/kanji-data) —
  KANJIDIC readings/strokes, Waller levels, WaniKani radical names.
- [scriptin/jmdict-simplified](https://github.com/scriptin/jmdict-simplified) —
  English JMdict JSON used for example words; CC BY-SA 4.0 / EDRDG dictionary terms.

These are derived datasets. Do not treat the generated JSON as public-domain; keep
attribution when redistributing and consult each upstream project for exact terms.
JLPT levels are community estimates, not official Japan Foundation lists.
